Empirical Research Plan: 19-Year-Old Insurance Cut-Off and Health-Care Utilization (NHIS 1997-2008)

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. Identification Strategy
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Method: Fuzzy Regression Discontinuity Design (FRD) with Age as the running variable and a discontinuity at the 19-th birthday.

Rationale
• The institutional rule that dependents lose eligibility for parents’ private insurance at age 19 creates a sharp jump in the probability of being insured but does not deterministically set coverage to zero → fuzzy, not sharp.
• NHIS is a repeated cross-section; FRD does not require panel data.
• FRD delivers a Local Average Treatment Effect (LATE) for individuals “just” on either side of age 19—exactly the policy margin of interest.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
2. Treatment and Control Definition
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Running variable:   age_i (in years). Define 𝑟_i = age_i – 19, so the cut-off is r = 0.

Treatment indicator (endogenous):   INSURE_i = 1 if individual reports any private, employer, or public health-insurance coverage; 0 otherwise.

Instrument / cut-off dummy:         Z_i = 1{age_i ≥ 19}.

Local control group: Individuals with r_i < 0 but close to 0 (e.g., ages 17.5–18.99).
Local treatment group: Individuals with r_i ≥ 0 but close to 0 (e.g., ages 19.00–20.49).

Outcome variables (Y_i):
• DOCVIS_i   – number of doctor/clinic visits in past 12 months
• HOSP_i     – indicator or count of hospital stays
• ER_i       – indicator of any ER use
Controls (X_i): gender, race, region, calendar year FE, family income categories.

Bandwidth: Start with ±24 months (ages 17–21), vary from ±12 to ±36 months in robustness checks.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
3. Key Identifying Assumptions and Plausibility
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
A1. Continuity of Potential Outcomes at the Cut-off  
   Potential utilization in the absence of insurance changes smoothly with age.  
   Plausibility: Nothing besides insurance eligibility changes discretely exactly on the 19-th birthday; driver’s license, voting, military enlistment, etc. happen earlier (16–18) or later (21).

A2. No Precise Manipulation of the Running Variable  
   Individuals cannot misreport age in NHIS to stay 18 forever.  
   Plausibility: Age in NHIS is interviewer-recorded; heaping at integers is uniform across ages.

A3. First-Stage Relevance / Monotonicity  
   Crossing 19 must significantly reduce insurance take-up, and no one gains insurance because of the cut-off.  
   Plausibility: Employer-sponsored plans do not suddenly appear at 19; public-insurance eligibility (Medicaid/CHIP) also weakens. Historical evidence shows ~25–30 p.p. drop.

A4. Stable Unit Treatment Value (SUTVA)  
   No spillovers from one individual’s coverage status to another in the neighborhood of the cut-off. Seems reasonable at the individual level.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
4. Main Threats and Mitigations
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
T1. Confounding Life-Cycle Changes at 19  
   • 19 often coincides with high-school completion, college entry, and labor-market entry.  
Mitigation:  
   – Control flexibly for education enrollment status where available.  
   – Include year-of-survey FE to absorb macro shocks that correlate with schooling cohorts.  
   – Show continuity of covariates (school enrollment, employment, marital status) at age 19.

T2. Discrete Age Reporting (Age in Years)  
   • Age heaping at integer values can blur the location of the true threshold.  
Mitigation:  
   – Use half-year bins: define age 18.5-18.99 as below, 19.0-19.49 as above.  
   – Apply the “donut RD” (drop those exactly age 19) as robustness.  
   – Show McCrary density test on age in months where NHIS publicly reports quarter-year age.

T3. Weak First Stage in Sub-Samples  
   • Insurance gaps smaller among low-income children on Medicaid.  
Mitigation:  
   – Report first-stage F-statistics.  
   – Run separate FRD by income; pool only if first stage > 10 in each.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
5. R Code Outline
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```r
# -----------------------------------------------
# 0. Packages
# -----------------------------------------------
library(data.table)   # fast data handling
library(fixest)       # fast IV estimation
library(rdrobust)     # RD routines
library(ggplot2)

# -----------------------------------------------
# 1. Load and Prepare Data
# -----------------------------------------------
nhis <- fread("NHIS_1997_2008.csv")   # columns: age, insure, docvis, hosp, er, gender, race, income, year

# running variable
nhis[, age_center := age - 19]

# local window (±2 yrs)
nhis_local <- nhis[age_center >= -2 & age_center <= 2]

# treatment (endogenous) and instrument
nhis_local[, insure := as.integer(insurance_status == "covered")]
nhis_local[, treat19 := as.integer(age >= 19)]

# controls
ctrls <- c("factor(gender)", "factor(race)", "factor(region)", "factor(year)", "factor(income_cat)")

# -----------------------------------------------
# 2. Main FRD (2SLS) Specification
# -----------------------------------------------
form_main <- as.formula(
  paste("docvis ~ poly(age_center, 3) +", paste(ctrls, collapse = " + "),
        "| treat19 + poly(age_center, 3) +", paste(ctrls, collapse = " + "))
)
est_docvis <- feols(form_main, data = nhis_local, vcov = "HC1")
summary(est_docvis)

# hospital stays outcome
form_hosp <- update(form_main, hosp ~ .)
est_hosp <- feols(form_hosp, data = nhis_local, vcov = "HC1")

# -----------------------------------------------
# 3. First-Stage Check
# -----------------------------------------------
fs <- feols(insure ~ poly(age_center,3) + treat19 + 
              paste(ctrls, collapse=" + "), data=nhis_local, vcov="HC1")
summary(fs)

# -----------------------------------------------
# 4. Robustness: rdrobust with varying bandwidths
# -----------------------------------------------
rd_main <- rdrobust(y = nhis$docvis, x = nhis$age_center, c = 0, fuzzy = nhis$treat19)
summary(rd_main)

# narrower window ±1 year
rd_narrow <- rdrobust(y = nhis$docvis, x = nhis$age_center,
                      c = 0, h = 1, fuzzy = nhis$treat19)
summary(rd_narrow)

# Placebo cut-off at 20
placebo <- rdrobust(y = nhis$docvis, x = nhis$age_center - 1,
                    c = 0, fuzzy = nhis$treat19)   # shift cut-off
summary(placebo)

# -----------------------------------------------
# 5. Covariate Balance Plot
# -----------------------------------------------
covs <- c("female", "college_enroll", "income_cat")
for (v in covs){
  ggplot(nhis_local, aes(x = age_center, y = get(v))) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.3) + geom_smooth(method = "loess") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, lty = 2) +
    labs(title = paste("RD Covariate Check:", v))
}
```

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
6. Expected Results
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Economic intuition: Losing insurance at 19 increases out-of-pocket prices and should reduce discretionary utilization (doctor visits, preventative care). Emergency or unavoidable hospital admissions are less price-elastic.

Priors:
• Doctor visits: −0.25 to −0.40 visits per year (≈10-15 % drop) for the LATE group.  
• Hospital stays: small negative, −0.01 stays (≈4-5 % drop), possibly not statistically significant.  
• ER visits: ambiguous; could rise (substitution toward ER) or fall (overall lower demand).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (RD)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
C1. Continuity of potential outcomes at cut-off ............. 0.8  
C2. No manipulation of running variable (McCrary test) ...... 1.0  
C3. First-stage relevance (F-stat > 10) ..................... 1.0  
C4. Covariate balance across cut-off ........................ 0.8  
C5. Robust to bandwidth & polynomial choices ................ 0.8  

Overall ≈ 4.4 / 5.
